newsitem.title: INDIA: India can look to supply Malaysia sugar market.
newsitem.headline: India can look to supply Malaysia sugar market.

text.p: Malaysia, a net importer of raw sugar, is looking to broaden its sources of supplies, and offers trading opportunities to India with its excess stocks, a senior Malaysian official said on Tuesday.

"Opportunities are not lacking for countries like India and other producers to explore the Malaysian market," said Mohammad Bin Nik, principal assistant director of the Malaysian Domestic Trade and Consumer Affairs Ministry.

India is expected to produce a record 16.45 million tonnes of sugar in 1995/96 (October-September), up sharply from 14.6 million in 1994/95. Output for 1996/97 has been forecast by the industry at about 15 million tonnes.
India consumes about 13 million tonnes every year.
Nik said Malaysian sugar consumption was growing five percent annually. But its geographical conditions were not suitable for domestic cultivation.
He said more Malaysian farmland was being diverted to industrial use due to rapid economic development, making it difficult to increase land under sugarcane cultivation.
"Therefore sugar exporting countries should not ignore the fact that Malaysia can be one of the markets that they would be looking at," Nik said.
Malaysia produces about 91,000 tonnes of raw sugar every year. It imports nearly 80 percent of its raw sugar requirements from Australia, Fiji and Thailand.
Malaysia's domestic consumption of refined sugar increased to 861,266 tonnes in 1995 from 672,205 tonnes in 1990.
"Consumption of sugar had shown a steady increase since 1990 and is anticipated to increase to about one million tonnes by the year 2000," Nik said.
He said Malaysia's per capita consumption of sugar in 1995 was about 42 kg compared to world per capita consumption of nearly 200 kg.
"Thus, one can see the consumption growth potential of sugar in Malaysia," Nik said.
In 1995, Malaysia produced 1.09 million tonnes of refined sugar, up from 1.05 million in 1994. It exported 198,026 tonnes of refined sugar last year, down from 250,927 tonnes in 1994, he said.
